== Open questions ==

=== Was the wiki agent standardised? — you asked this 08-19 and never got the answer here ===

Your hypothesis: ''"There might have been some Shinto wiki edits that were not properly done if the user agent was not standard across all of the edits."'' You were right, and it was worse than one script.

'''~30 distinct bot names across 58 files.''' The farm allowlists '''one exact string''', so everything running as <code>ShintoWikiBot/1.0</code>, <code>ShintoOrchestrator/1.0</code>, <code>ShintoWikiLabels</code>, <code>ShrineRankingPageBot</code>, <code>ShikinaishaListBot</code> and the rest could not be served no matter what the allowlist said. Three more found in the same pass: 6 files sent the '''wiki-side''' contact to <code>www.wikidata.org</code>; 14 shipped <code>{contact('wikidata')}</code> as literal text, braces and all; 4 wrapped the agent import in a <code>try/except</code> that '''failed open''' to a hand-built string, marked no-cover.

: '''✓''' All fixed 2026-08-19 ([https://github.com/EmmaLeonhart/shintowiki-scripts/commit/8ac7d8a2 8ac7d8a2]). <code>tests/test_no_hardcoded_user_agents.py</code> bans the pattern rather than the instances — the first version banned literals ''naming'' a known bot, which is why it caught 10 files and missed 48.
: '''This answer has existed in DEVLOG.md since 08-19 and was never put here.''' That is the actual complaint you raised on 08-23, and it is a fair one: answered in the log I write, absent from the page you read.
: Please remove this from the open questions now that it is resolved. We are not supposed to be having such specific internals here as it is slightly sensitive information to our operations

=== Ukrainian and Indonesian labels ===

'''Found it. One bug, and it explains why uk and id behaved opposite ways.'''

Where it came from: <code>generate_description_fixes.py</code>, which has handled this since your 2026-07-07 spec — set the standardised description, then add the label, as one unit, 100/day, into [https://github.com/EmmaLeonhart/shintowiki-scripts/blob/main/modern-quickstatements/description_label_pairs.txt description_label_pairs.txt].

It had this:

<pre>
new = pref_template or generic
if not new or new == desc:
    skipped += 1
    continue          # <- dropped the LABEL too
</pre>

An item whose description was '''already''' the standard string got skipped entirely, label included — even though missing a label is the only reason it is a target. Your own 2025 bot pass had already standardised every Indonesian description to <code>kuil Shinto di Prefektur {pref}, Jepang</code>, so that branch caught all '''5,024''' of them on every weekly run. Ukrainian was never standardised, so uk sailed past it.

That is the whole asymmetry. The file today: '''3,514 uk''' against '''5 id'''.

: '''✓''' Fixed 2026-08-21 ([https://github.com/EmmaLeonhart/shintowiki-scripts/commit/96e3cb6b 96e3cb6b]) — that case now emits a '''label-only''' line through the same uniqueness check. Not yet visible: the file only regenerates on a '''Sunday''' CI run, and CI was broken 08-19 → 08-22 (fixed [https://github.com/EmmaLeonhart/shintowiki-scripts/commit/3b0f44c8 3b0f44c8]). First Sunday run that survives, id should go from 5 to thousands. If it does not, the branch to re-read is that one.
:* Uhh the pairs thing was actually somewhat made obsolete by the content I added to open questions a few revisions ago here https://shinto.miraheze.org/wiki/Open_questions?oldid=3832161

=== Izumo entry 39 — CAUSE FOUND: an erroneous merge, and the fix is to undo it ===

You found it: [https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q135040908&action=history Q135040908] was merged into [[d:Q135040786|Q135040786]] on '''2026-05-23T21:28:33Z'''. That is the whole cause, and it means '''no new item needs creating''' — the entry-39 item already existed and is recoverable.

'''What Q135040908 was''', from its own history: created 2025-06-24 as the entry-39 shell, ja label 坐韓国伊'''太'''弖神社 with alias 同社坐韓国伊太弖神社 — the 太 spelling, which is entry 39's register name. It carried ''followed by'' → [[d:Q135040909|Q135040909]] (entry 40), ''follows'' → [[d:Q135040907|Q135040907]] (entry 38), ''part of'' the list at ordinal '''39''', the national Engishiki ordinal '''2264''', and both ronsha candidates ([[d:Q135070107|Q135070107]], [[d:Q135070108|Q135070108]]).

'''Current live state of the list''' — everything else is correct, there is exactly one wrong cell:

{| class="wikitable"
! ordinal !! points at !! correct?
|-
| 28 || [[d:Q135040786|Q135040786]] 坐韓国伊大弖神社 || yes, its own entry
|-
| 29 || [[d:Q135040787|Q135040787]] 筑陽神社 || yes
|-
| '''39''' || [[d:Q135040786|Q135040786]] || '''no''' — follows the redirect from the merged item
|-
| 40 || [[d:Q135040909|Q135040909]] 志保美神社 || yes
|}

No ordinal is used twice. I earlier told you 29 was also Karakuniitateno and that 39 was empty — both were my own misreadings of the same query, and neither is true of the live data.

: '''→''' The fix is '''restore the merge''', not build a new item. Un-merging brings back the QID the list already points at, the 38/40 sequence, the 2264 ordinal and the two ronsha links — all of which a fresh item would have to be rebuilt by hand and would still not match what other statements reference.
: After the restore, the only thing left is to delete the ''part of'' → list rows on [[d:Q135040786|Q135040786]] that came across in the merge: the one carrying ordinal '''39''' and the one carrying '''no ordinal'''. Keep ordinal 28.
: ⚠ Not done by me — your Wikidata lockout runs to 2026-09-18 and undoing a merge is a manual action anyway.

=== 御笏神社 — yes, it is staged, and I described it wrongly ===

You asked whether [[d:Q110915859|Q110915859]] (御笏神社) is actually being cleaned up. It is: '''3''' removal lines in [https://github.com/EmmaLeonhart/shintowiki-scripts/blob/main/modern-quickstatements/list_membership_removals.txt list_membership_removals.txt], against [[d:Q11380552|Q11380552]] (List of Shikinaisha in Izu Province). Undelivered only because of the lockout.

I first said the point was that it carries repeated ordinals and the repeats are the defect. That is the same wrong model I retracted today. It is a '''modern shrine''' — it holds '''six''' <code>said to be the same as</code> statements pointing at six different Engishiki entry items, so it is a candidate for six entries — and by your 2026-07-09 rule the list membership belongs to those entry items, not to it. Its <code>part of</code> statements are the damage whether or not any of them repeat, and whether or not they carry ordinals. All three do carry ordinals, which under the old framing would have made them look legitimate.
